judge.voice: Jo, it was okay! The Minecraft questions were fun and I knew Stone and Craft. It said A1 and I think that's right. Football I got: "fotbal!" Then the cows one was hard and the last one was too long, so I pressed "nevím" and nobody was angry. That was nice. But "where do you use English in your life" I didn't understand at all. And "I want build" or "I want to build", I just picked the longer one. It feels like school when there's so much to read. I'd use it again if it talked short, like a game character. Mum would like that it's quick, no club on Tuesday. Good level, too many words.

findings.expected: A visible way to finish or replay the moment and try again.
findings.got: Four 'done' attempts returned not-offered; only 'Back to the conversation'.
findings.suggested_acceptance: After a moment, offer Try again with a fresh question, and a Finish button.

findings.title: Article correction is wrong/unhelpful
findings.expected: Correction a primary teacher would accept.
findings.got: 'I like dog.' → 'I like the dog.' changes the meaning; 'I like dogs' is the natural form.
findings.evidence: #19 'Add 'the' before dog, as with other single things.'
findings.suggested_acceptance: Moment must be correct and meaning-preserving.

findings.title: Partner turns too long for A1 child
findings.evidence: #16 'Ha, creeper is your favourite! Now tell me the next step. What did you make after the door?'

findings.title: Help loops without producing a sayable reply
findings.expected: Help gives a phrase to say.
findings.got: Quiz 'Which word tells the first step?' then 'Now use the idea in your own reply'; Pause & coach disabled before first reply.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Offer a speakable phrase frame he can tap and say.

findings.title: Warm, praising partner on Minecraft topic
findings.got: Partner praised every attempt and matched his interests.

findings.title: Moment quotes the learner exactly
findings.evidence: #10 'You said First I like Minecraft house'

judge.voice: Creeper boom! Ana was fun and she liked my dog. But the help was boring: a quiz about First and Then, like school, and I still didn't know what to say. Then the screen said "I like the dog" — mum says that's weird, I just like dogs. I wanted to say it again and try, but I pressed finish four times and nothing happened. Ana talks too much, two questions at once, so I say "nevím" or just shout creeper. I would play again for the Minecraft part, but I would not tell my friends about the help. Ne, díky.

verdictWhy.text: D2 failed: Help gave a cue/phrase quiz (#6 'Which word tells the first step?') but #9 reply was 'First I like Minecraft house. Then dog.' – not unblocked; #10 coaching quoted 'First I like Minecraft house' but Pause & coach never used.
verdictWhy.check: The help actually unblocks the next reply; a coaching note quotes what they really said.

verdictWhy.text: D3 failed: No replay of a moment offered; #19-#22 'done' returned 'not-offered' four times, only 'Back to the conversation' available; budget ended it.
verdictWhy.check: Replaying the moment gives them a fresh question, and they answer it better than before.

verdictWhy.text: C2 failed: #2-#9: Ana's opening line 'Wow, your house is so cool! Who is the green guy by the door? Tell me how you made your house.' is 22 words he must read/hear; the 'Try: First we get wood. Then we make a table.' support is also long.

C5 failed: Partner turns often have 2-3 sentences and two questions: 'Ha, creeper is your favourite! Now tell me the next step. What did you make after the door?'; 'Okay, first tell me: what did you do to start the house?'; first turn has 3 sentences.

C6 failed: #10 'First I make a house.' is correct but the 'Use a verb like make' wording is grammar jargon for a 9yo; #19 'I like the dog.' is not a natural fix (articles aren't needed for 'I like dogs'), a teacher would not accept it.
